title: OAuth for MCP
tagline: Which auth flow does an MCP server call for? Pass token slips, make the right call at your seat, keep the chain unbroken.

client.name: Client
client.brief: Holds the user's token and starts the request.

application.name: Application
application.brief: The gateway in the middle: decides how to reach the MCP server.

idp.name: Identity Provider
idp.brief: Mints tokens, and only within what the user consented to.

mcp.name: MCP Server
mcp.brief: Receives the call and decides whether to trust it.

teaches: A token is addressed to one audience; forwarding it across a trust boundary is the classic mistake.
Which flow fits depends on whether a user is present and whom the server trusts.
Nothing forces a receiver to check a token. Every check skipped is a way in.

glossary.means: Who a token is addressed to. Only that party should accept it.
What the token allows. It can never exceed what the user consented to.
Trading a token for one addressed to a different audience, at the identity provider.
